newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU agrees "green" label for eco-friendly fridges.
newsitem.headline: EU agrees "green" label for eco-friendly fridges.

text.p: Fridge and freezer makers who use no ozone-damaging chemicals and make quieter and more energy-efficient machines than than their rivals may now qualify for EU eco-labels on their wares, the European Commission said.

"This will make it easier for consumers who want to choose goods with a reduced environmental impact to make an informed choice by selecting the product with the flower logo from a range of products and brands," the EU executive said on Friday.

Manufacturers must apply for permission to use the logo, a flower with the EU's 12 stars as petals around a stylised letter 'E', which is granted only to those products which meet certain energy efficiency and other environmental requirements.

Fridges have traditionally used chlorofluorocarbons and related chemicals (CFCs and HCFCs) in their refrigerants and insulation, making the sector a major contributor to atmospheric releases of the volatile gases which damage the Earth's protective ozone layer.
These will not be permitted in products carrying the EU eco-label, a development which delighted campaigners from the environmental group Greenpeace.

"The Commission's decision is a major victory for the environment as it rules out labelling any refrigerator that uses HCFCs or HCFC 134-a as environmentally acceptable," Greenpeace climate campaigner Bill Hare said in a statement.

"HCFCs destroy the ozone layer and HCFCs are very potent greenhouse gases...There is no excuse for the ongoing use of these dangerous substances when environmentally safer technologies are available and commercially proven," Hare said.

Hare's reference to "greenhouse" gases relates to the widely held theory that the Earth's atmosphere is warming as a result of excessive, human-generated emissions of a variety of energy-trapping gases.
